# Exact anisotropic heat proof of quasiconvexity for G

Research date: 15 October 2026. Worker: nonlinear_qc / phase_geometry.
Repository source pin: `b7cada92d2eb304578be5ed974f1e44b10a89928`.

## Result and status

The particular retained quartic G is quasiconvex at **every** affine background.
The proof uses a rational closed two-form and a rational positive semidefinite
Gram identity for the full compatible second-jet density. No prescribed phase,
Cartesian partial minimum, frequency truncation, or numerical search conclusion
is a premise. The same G is non-polyconvex and lies on an acoustic boundary.

This is a complete internal proof with independently checkable finite algebra.
Root independently reconstructed the JSON identity, all closedness equations,
and the positive reduced LDL pivots using a separate Fraction-based checker.
That is same-team checking, not external mathematical review. Historical novelty
and external correctness review are UNKNOWN. The full nine-coefficient
left-SO(2)-invariant cone and the general planar Morrey implication remain open.

The heat/exact-two-form method is prior mathematics, including
[Bruno and Pasqualotto, arXiv:2608.06367v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06367v1),
Sections 2 and 3, and the pinned N740/N794 capital. The new load-bearing object
here is a concrete exact certificate for G. The positive Fstar-orbit obstruction
and the Dacorogna-Marcellini orbit exclusion are addressed separately; no claim
that a new general analytic method was invented is made.

## 1. Integrand, domain and complete statement

For `A=[[a,b],[c,d]]`, set

    u=a^2+c^2,    v=b^2+d^2,    j=ad-bc,
    G(A)=3(u+v-2j)^2+(35/24)u^2+j^2-(5/2)ju.             (1.1)

Theorem. For every bounded Lipschitz domain `Omega` in R2, every constant
matrix `B in R^(2x2)`, and every `phi in W_0^(1,4)(Omega,R2)`,

    integral_Omega G(B+Dphi) >= |Omega| G(B).             (1.2)

In particular, this proves the usual quasiconvexity condition, whose test class
is W0^(1,infinity). The periodic counterpart also holds: for every periodic
`phi in W^(1,4)(T2,R2)` and every B,

    <G(B+Dphi)> >= G(B).                                 (1.3)

All input frequencies, nonlinear resonances, amplitudes and phases are included.

## 2. The exact finite certificate

The portable proof object is `G_EXACT_HEAT_CERTIFICATE.json`, SHA-256

    4004e6144335150a5b3569dfb7b4d0b836f2776

# Exact compensated heat certificate for G: independent analytic reconstruction

Date: 2026-10-15. This review reconstructs a newly routed specific-polynomial proof, including an independent exact verifier. It is an internal mathematical result and scoped same-team review. External correctness, historical novelty and physical capability remain UNKNOWN. No full left-invariant quartic-cone implication is inferred.

Certificate read: `workers/nonlinear_qc/G_EXACT_HEAT_CERTIFICATE.json`, SHA256 **4004e6144335150a5b3569dfb7b4d0b836f2776497c271e7f31b2faf52830000**. The producer verifier was read to interpret its conventions; it was not imported or executed. The independently authored `verify_G_certificate_adversarial.py` reconstructs the certificate directly from JSON with Fraction arithmetic and SymPy polynomial identities; all five check groups pass. No acquisition/search/numerical candidate is a proof premise.

## 1. Exact statement and matrix convention

For A=[[a,b],[c,d]], set u=a²+c², v=b²+d² and j=ad−bc. The specific homogeneous quartic is

    G(A)=3(u+v−2j)²+(35/24)u²+j²−(5/2)ju.

The certificate supplies a global polynomial identity and PSD rational Gram implying that G is quasiconvex: for every B∈R²ˣ², bounded domain Ω, and φ∈W0¹,⁴(Ω;R²),

    ∫Ω G(B+Dφ) ≥ |Ω|G(B).

Here W0¹,⁴ is the closure of compactly supported smooth functions. A Lipschitz boundary is sufficient but is not needed for the zero-extension argument with this definition. Smooth compact affine-Dirichlet tests in particular satisfy the ordinary quasiconvexity inequality.

## 2. What exact algebra was checked

The certificate orders the matrix entries as (a,b,c,d), and the compatible second jets as

    h=(φ1_xx,φ1_xy,φ1_yy,φ2_xx,φ2_xy,φ2_yy).

Thus, for A=B+Dφ,

    A_x=(h₀,h₁,h₃,h₄), A_y=(h₁,h₂,h₄,h₅).

The repeated mixed derivatives are essential; arbitrary unrelated first jets of a matrix field would not supply this identity. Let Z have entries A_i h_k with the A index outermost. The exact identity is

    ZᵀQZ = d₁ D²G(A)[A_x,A_x] + d₂ D²G(A)[A_y,A_y]
               + Ω_A(A_x,A_y),
    d₁=4897/5000, d₂=5103/5000.
